At Atominvest, you’ll be working on something very exciting: the future of work, investments and sustainability/ ethical investing for the world’s best investors and delivering a positive impact through this. Based on the growth we are experiencing, we think we’re on to something big.

It won’t be easy. Joining a scale up business is an amazing and rewarding challenge, pushing well beyond the boundaries of natural growth cycles. You’ll move quicker than feels comfortable and be brilliant at continually re-prioritizing what must get done to keep Atominvest growing year over year at the pace of the best SaaS companies on the planet.

We’ve gone from zero to ten, now we’re looking to go from ten to one hundred!

About the role

Hi, I'm Thomas, VP Engineering at Atominvest. This is the hire I'm most excited about, so I wanted to tell you about it myself.

You'll own the platform our clients run on and build the AI development harness our engineers work in day to day. That work runs from infrastructure to application code, so we're looking for an experienced engineer with breadth across both, and depth in at least one. Together, it's what lets a small, lean team, working alongside AI agents, ship like a much bigger one.

 

By platform, we mean everything our product and our engineers stand on: infrastructure, security, test automation, developer experience, and the agent pipelines that run through all of them. It's a broad, hands-on role. You'll write infrastructure as code for a new service one day and address network vulnerabilities the next, then enhance our AI development harness and release a new feature, all within the same month.

 

You might be a platform engineer who loves shipping product, or a full-stack engineer who has run serious production infrastructure. Either works.

As deployments grow more complex, the team needs your depth in infrastructure and distributed systems. You'll strengthen the architecture and make the design decisions the platform will rest on for years. Those decisions should leave room to grow, because future products may bring much larger volumes of data than we handle today.

It has to stay dependable while we do it. Our software needs to be available around the clock, every day of the year, and data integrity is critical. Our clients use Atominvest to report to their own investors, so a wrong number matters as much as an outage. Security, reliability and audit-readiness matter too. If you enjoy getting those right without slowing everything else down, you'll find plenty of fun things to work on.

The machine that builds the product

We're becoming AI-native. Agents do more and more of the mechanical work of writing code, and engineers build the machine that builds the product: the architecture, the specs, the limits agents work within, and the evals that tell us whether their output is right.

I think that moves an engineer's leverage upstream. When code is cheap, the scarce things are judgement and understanding. Which problem is worth solving? What does good look like for the person using it? Is the output actually right? Did what we shipped help? The best engineers I've worked with always solved the end problem, with code as the medium. Now that's most of the job.

That's why product and user understanding sit at the centre of how we work. An engineer who knows our clients' workflows can point agents at the right problem and spot when the result is subtly wrong. Without that, agents just build the wrong thing faster.

Your part is the AI development harness that makes this safe. That means sandboxed environments with synthetic data, scoped and audited access to logs and alerts, and evals and validation gates in CI. It also means firm lines, enforced by tooling, that keep production deploys and secrets in human hands, and client data out of reach of development agents.

You'll also build the agent orchestration pipelines that run in three places: in how we build software, in AI workflows inside the product our clients use, and in the internal tools our implementation team uses to onboard and configure clients.

What you'll do

Build the machine that builds the product

Most of your time goes here.

  • Build our AI development harness. Self-service infrastructure, a reproducible development environment, and the sandboxes, guardrails and evals that let agents take on more of the work safely, with results we can measure.

  • Automate quality. Build the QA automation pipeline: automated tests, validation gates and release checks that give us confidence in every change, including the ones agents write.

  • Orchestrate agents across the business. Build pipelines that run agents reliably and safely in our product workflows and our internal implementation tools, not just in engineering.

Own the platform

  • Own our infrastructure. We're migrating to ECS. You'll strengthen our ECS architecture, see the move through in safe, reversible stages, bring every resource under infrastructure as code, and retire the old deployment model.

  • Build security into the platform. Tenant-scoped credentials, per-tenant secrets, least-privilege access, and the audit trail that SOC 2 and our clients' security teams expect.

  • Make production observable. Set up the monitoring, alerting and tracing we rely on, and build playbooks for on-call and incident response which is shared amongst the team.

Work across the stack

  • Make the application changes the harness needs, such as synthetic data, test hooks and the specs agents work from.

  • Ship product. Pick up application work in TypeScript and React alongside the team. Over time, you'll learn the codebase as well as the platform it runs on.

  • Grow the team around you. Write the design notes and runbooks, pair with and review the work of other engineers, and mentor those who want to grow into infrastructure, so the platform never depends on one person.

Your first six months

  • Get the first parts of "the machine" running, and show that they make the team faster without lowering quality.

  • At the moment all of our end to end testing is done manually by our Product team. That's a massive manual overhead that bottlenecks our product development. You'll help build our AI-powered QA automation pipeline, so every change, whether a person or an agent wrote it, is tested automatically before it reaches clients.

  • Strengthen the ECS architecture and complete the move with no disruption to clients.

  • Get the platform fully into code, with tenant isolation and least privilege designed in.

  • Put in place the monitoring and on-call foundations the team will build on.

How you'll work

You'll own this area rather than work through a ticket queue. You'll decide what to build and when it's good enough, write your decisions down so others can challenge them, and tell us when something isn't worth doing. You'll work closely with Product from the start of significant work, because the platform exists to serve clients and the engineers building for them.

You and I will work together every day. We'll shape the technical direction together and think through the hard calls, and you'll have a direct line to every decision that affects your work. I'll back your judgement, and I'll expect you to push back when you think I'm wrong.

This is an individual contributor role, but we expect you to multiply the team: leading different areas at different times, and delivering through others as well as through your own work.

You'll probably enjoy this if

  • You'd rather build a platform properly than keep patching one.

  • You're product-minded. You've probably worked at a startup or scale-up, or even founded something yourself. Seeing your work out in the world, solving real problems, is what motivates you. You ask who a change is for before you ask how to build it.

  • You already work this way. Agents write much of your code, and your time goes on design, specs and judging the output. You've built AI tooling for yourself, and probably for others on your team.

  • You get satisfaction from making other engineers faster.

  • You're comfortable writing Terraform, an API endpoint and an answer to a client's security questionnaire in the same week.

  • You've been the person others come to with hard problems, and you've changed your mind publicly when the evidence said so.

This probably isn't for you if

  • You want a pure DevOps or SRE role.

  • You want to manage people right now. These opportunities might exist in the future, but for now we're small, lean and as flat as possible.

What you'll bring

Very few people match every line. If most of this describes you, we'd like to hear from you.

  • Deep, hands-on AWS. Several years running production workloads on ECS or EKS, with a solid grasp of IAM, networking and Lambda.

  • Infrastructure as code as a habit, with Terraform or CloudFormation, including bringing existing hand-built resources under code.

  • Scaling distributed systems. You've taken systems through real growth in load and data, and can teach others what you learnt.

  • Single-tenant SaaS experience. You know the isolation trade-offs and how to keep one client's data and credentials away from another's.

  • Security and compliance as part of engineering: least privilege, secrets management, and evidence for SOC 2 or ISO 27001.

  • Production experience: on-call, incidents, post-mortems, and observability tooling such as Datadog, Grafana or Honeycomb.

  • Full-stack product building. Senior TypeScript and Node.js, plus React, with a track record of shipping features end to end yourself, not just supporting the people who do.

  • Test automation and CI/CD. You've designed pipelines that test at the right levels and release safely, and you keep them fast and simple.

  • Tooling you've built for AI agents, not just used: agent configuration and orchestration, MCP servers or similar integrations, evals, automated review.

Our stack

TypeScript, Node.js, React and MongoDB Atlas, running on AWS. CircleCI and Bitbucket. AI coding agents are part of everyday work. You don't need experience of all of these.

How we hire

We want to see how you actually work, so there are no whiteboard puzzles.

  1. Screening call with me (20 minutes)

  2. Competencies interview with me (30 minutes)

  3. Technical deep dive with a few of our engineers (90 minutes)

  4. Culture fit interview with our CEO, Hemal (30 minutes)

I'll be your main point of contact throughout. You'll know what to expect before each stage, and if we don't make an offer, I'll give you feedback.

data.title: Staff Data Engineer (AI Data Platform)
data.description:
UFORCE exists to make aggression unaffordable.

Founded in Ukraine and headquartered in London, UFORCE is a defence-technology company with operations across Europe, the United States and Asia.

UFORCE builds uncrewed vessels, ground robotics and aircraft, autonomy software, and the command-and-control layer that operates them together. Each platform is deployable on its own, and stronger as part of the system. Its product lines include the MAGURA family of uncrewed surface vessels, the NEMESIS family of strike platforms, the LIUT family of ground robotic platforms, and counter-UAS systems.

About the role

The Staff Data Engineer (AI Data Platform) will design, build and operate the data platform that makes UFORCE’s operational data usable for AI model training and validation.

You will connect diverse data sources—from high-frequency telemetry and time series to imagery, video, documents and structured records—and make the resulting data discoverable, governed and reproducible. You will work hands-on across architecture, pipelines, data quality and platform operations, while helping other engineers and partner teams make sound technical decisions.

This is a staff-level individual contributor role for someone who combines strong engineering judgment with a practical approach to delivery. You will partner with ML, product, engineering, field and security teams to build a platform that works for real use cases and operating constraints. Model research and model performance decisions remain with the accountable ML and product owners.

What you’ll do

  • Design and deliver a data platform for ingesting, storing, discovering and preparing heterogeneous data for approved analytics and ML workflows.

  • Build reliable batch and streaming pipelines for priority data sources, with validation, schema evolution, retries, backfills, replay and appropriate handling of failed data.

  • Preserve the context needed to understand and trace data, including timestamps, source identity, format versions and provenance where available.

  • Establish data contracts, metadata, interfaces and ownership boundaries that make data easier to find, understand and use across teams.

  • Enable reproducible training and evaluation datasets, including source and transformation versions, labels, filters and split definitions.

  • Build data-quality checks for issues such as missing data, corruption, duplication and temporal misalignment. Work with ML partners to surface coverage, sampling and leakage risks.

  • Make data rights, classification, retention, permitted use and access restrictions visible and actionable.

  • Design for the environments the work requires, which may include cloud, on-premises, sovereign or disconnected deployments.

  • Instrument and operate data workflows with clear visibility into health, freshness, quality, throughput and cost. Document failure handling, recovery and operational ownership.

  • Apply appropriate access controls, encryption, auditability and data-handling practices in partnership with security and other stakeholders.

  • Lead technical decisions across teams, communicate trade-offs and risks, mentor engineers, and deliver reusable components in small, reviewable increments.

What success looks like

  • A coherent platform architecture and incremental roadmap support priority AI and product use cases, with clear interfaces and ownership.

  • Priority data sources are ingested reliably and traceably, with agreed measures for completeness, freshness, quality and recovery.

  • Approved datasets are discoverable, governed and reproducible from source data through transformations to training and evaluation outputs.

  • ML teams can assess data quality, provenance and known limitations before using a dataset, and issues can be traced back and corrected.

  • Platform workflows have actionable monitoring, documented recovery procedures and clear operational ownership.

  • Security, deployment and cost constraints are understood and incorporated into platform decisions.

  • Partner teams can use the platform effectively, and engineers are unblocked through clear designs, reusable tools and mentoring.

Success measures and numerical targets will be established with the hiring manager and partner teams once baselines and operating constraints are understood.

Required qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in data engineering, software engineering or a related field.

  • Data platform experience — designed, built and operated production data platforms or data-intensive systems end to end.

  • Staff-level technical leadership — led architectural decisions and cross-team delivery, mentored engineers and communicated clearly with stakeholders.

  • Hands-on engineering — strong Python and SQL skills, or equivalent, with experience in testing, code review and production-quality software.

  • Data pipelines — built reliable batch and streaming pipelines, including validation, schema evolution, retries, backfills and replay.

  • Data modalities — worked with structured or semi-structured data and at least one relevant modality, such as telemetry, time series, imagery, video or documents; understands provenance and temporal alignment.

  • ML data foundations — experience with storage, cataloguing, lineage, quality controls and reproducible datasets, including versioning, splits and leakage or sampling risks.

  • Platform operations — experience with observability, incident response, recovery, reliability and cost management.

  • Security and governance — practical knowledge of access controls, encryption, auditability, retention and sensitive-data handling.

Nice to have

  • Experience working with robotics, connected-device fleets or other operational systems that produce high-frequency or multimodal data.

  • Experience designing data systems for constrained connectivity, offline, air-gapped or sovereign environments.

  • Experience supporting defence, regulated or other security-sensitive customers.

The nature of combat has changed.

Tomorrow’s battlefield success depends on autonomy, speed, and adaptability.

And UFORCE is ready.

Are You?

data.title: Sustainability data advisor, financial services
data.description:
About Watershed

Watershed is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team.

We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us!

The role

Leading financial institutions like Carlyle Group, KKR, Ares, and BBVA use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive portfolio decarbonization.

We are looking for a customer-focused and analytically minded individual to join our Sustainability Data Advisory team in London, with a focus on financial institutions. You'll join a small team that operates like a startup within a startup at Watershed, working with some of the world's leading asset managers, private equity firms, banks, and insurers to accelerate their sustainability strategies.

You'll work directly with customers as a trusted advisor, leading measurement sessions and delivering advisory services that unlock the full value of our platform. You'll help customers measure financed emissions and use insights from their footprint to inform reporting and decision-making.

You will:

  • Advise teams at the world's largest financial institutions. Work directly with customers to measure financed emissions and strengthen their sustainable finance programs, supporting portfolio decarbonization and reporting across frameworks including TCFD, SFDR, CSRD, and LP reporting.

  • Deliver services that accelerate customer success. Lead measurement sessions and provide specialized advisory to help customers set up measurements, improve data quality, and unlock value from Watershed's platform. Support customers through emissions verification when needed.

  • Collaborate with science, engineering, and product teams to apply innovative measurement solutions, interpret the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF) standards, and help customers make informed choices about how to measure emissions across asset classes.

You might be a fit if you:

  • Have 4–6 years of experience in consulting, solutions engineering, another customer-facing role in sustainability. You are excited to work directly with customers to help them build world-class sustainability programs.

  • Have an understanding of PCAF methodology and experience applying it to financed emissions measurement.

  • Have experience working with financial institutions and understand how they use emissions to inform internal decision-making and sustainability strategies.

  • Are an excellent verbal and written communicator. You can communicate complex topics to technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Learn quickly and operate well in ambiguity. You are organized, systematic, and efficient, and you thrive in a high-volume environment.

  • Think clearly about complex problems and are comfortable using and speaking to data. You are meticulous and detail-obsessed.

  • Are passionate about solving climate change and excited to contribute to doing so at a fast-paced startup.

Fluency in multiple languages—English, French, German, or Spanish—is a nice to have.

This position requires working in person in our London office four days per week.

Must be willing to work from an office 4 days per week (except for remote roles)

Watershed has hub offices in San Francisco, New York, London, and Mexico City and satellite offices in Denver, Sydney, Paris, and Berlin. Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. Certain jobs are open to being remote and will be specifically noted on the jobs page and in the job description if so.

What’s the interview process like?

It starts the same for every candidate: getting to know the team members through 1 to 2 conversations about Watershed, your experience, and your interests. Next steps can vary by role, but usual next steps are a skill or experience interview (e.g. a coding interview for an engineer, a portfolio review for a designer, deeper experience call for other roles) which leads to a virtual or in person interview panel. We prioritize transparency and lack of surprise throughout the process.

What if I need accommodations for my interview?

At Watershed, we are dedicated to ensuring an inclusive recruitment process. We provide reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities, long-term conditions, mental health needs, religious observances, neurodivergence, or pregnancy-related support requirements. If you need assistance during your process, please contact your recruiter.

data.description:
ABOUT FLOCK

Road accidents kill and injure people, damage vehicles, and cost businesses fortunes. But traditional insurance does nothing to prevent them - it just pays out claims when they happen. At Flock, we’re changing that. Using telematics, AI, and real-time data, we proactively help our fleet customers prevent crashes. We obsessively focus on keeping drivers safe, and we put our money where our mouth is - paying out millions of pounds per year to fleets that get safer over time.

We were acquired by Admiral in May 2026. Now we combine the backing of the UK’s leading motor insurer with startup energy and speed. We’re growing fast with bigger plans than ever, and we’re hugely optimistic that our approach will save many more lives in the decade ahead.

We’re on a mission to make the world quantifiably safer. Join us!

We’re an AI-first business, so whatever the role, we want people who reach for AI by default, stay curious about what it can do, and use it to work faster and think bigger.

THE ROLE

Engineering Lead for the Acquisition team. You’ll report to our Head of Engineering. You’ll work closely with the PM to lead the team toward its goals, owning delivery, operational reliability and developer experience. You’ll ship production code and provide technical coaching and leadership to the engineers around you, not line management. You’ll also shape how the team uses AI tools and coding agents to ship faster without lowering the quality bar.

WHAT WE THINK IS MOST EXCITING ABOUT THE ROLE:

Lead a team building products that directly drive Flock’s growth

  • Own delivery and technical quality for the Acquisition team, working hand in hand with the PM to ship features that directly impact how fleets find and choose Flock.

  • Write high-quality, well-tested TypeScript and own end-to-end delivery to production

Partner with product to drive impact

  • Work closely with the PM, the Engineering Leadership Team and stakeholders to translate business goals into clear technical scope, success metrics and delivery plans.

Grow engineers around you

  • Lead by example through code, design discussions and pairing.

  • Coach and mentor engineers across the team to raise standards and share ownership of technical direction.

Shape how the team works, not just what it builds

  • Drive improvements to developer experience, CI/CD, observability and release practices that make the whole team faster and more confident.

  • Make pragmatic trade-offs that balance reliability, performance and cost across AWS services.

  • Decide how the team uses AI, from coding assistants to agent workflows in review and release, keeping engineering judgement where it matters.

Curious how we build the future of fleet insurance? Dive into our Product & Engineering Blog, packed with technical deep-dives, behind-the-scenes stories, and real insights from the team you’d be joining.

A LITTLE MORE ON WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING:

As an Engineering Lead at Flock you’ll own delivery and technical direction for the Acquisition team, co-leading with the PM to ship products that directly drive growth, while raising the bar for the engineers around you.

API-Driven Development

  • Integrate with and contribute to the development of RESTful APIs exposed via API Gateway.

Serverless & Cloud Infrastructure

  • Use your AWS experience (Lambda, API Gateway, SQS, EventBridge, DynamoDB, S3, CloudWatch) to support and extend the Acquisition team’s services and pipelines.

  • Work with infrastructure-as-code tools like Terraform or CDK for provisioning and managing cloud resources.

Collaboration & Agile Delivery

  • Co-own the team’s success with the PM, jointly leading projects from scoping and planning through to delivery and measuring impact.

  • Give engineers the space and ownership to lead projects themselves, asking the right questions to challenge their thinking and help them land on the right solution.

Code Quality & Technical Standards

  • Deliver high-quality, well-tested code and act as a force-multiplier, raising standards through code reviews, pairing and design discussions.

  • Champion practical testing, type-safe APIs and pragmatic patterns that shape long-term technical direction across the team.

  • Set the example on AI-assisted development and coach engineers on where it genuinely speeds the team up and where human judgement needs to stay in the loop.

Working closely with your PM, you’ll bring clarity to complex problems and help define sharply scoped, impactful deliverables. Your success won’t be measured by your own output alone, but by the output, quality and growth of the whole team around you.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING TO FLOCK:

ESSENTIAL

  • Proven ability to co-lead a team alongside a PM, taking joint ownership of delivery, quality and outcomes, not just your own output.

  • Strong hands-on engineering ability; comfortable shipping high-quality, well-tested TypeScript in production and holding the team to the same standard.

  • Significant experience with AWS and modern serverless (Lambda, API Gateway, SQS, EventBridge, DynamoDB, S3, CloudWatch) or other cloud platforms.

  • A pragmatic approach to technical decisions, balancing reliability, observability, performance and cost, and bringing engineers along on the reasoning.

  • Track record of raising engineering standards as a force-multiplier, through code reviews, pairing, design discussions and shaping long-term technical direction.

  • Strong communication skills; able to represent the team upwards and translate business goals into clear technical scope and delivery plans.

  • Experience improving developer experience, CI/CD, release practices and delivery cadence across a team.

  • Confident using AI development tools every day, with experience of helping a team adopt them without letting quality slip.

PREFERABLE

  • Experience aligning technical direction beyond your immediate team, working with senior stakeholders and other leads to shape how engineering works at a broader level.

  • Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code tools like Terraform or CDK, with a track record of improving operational resilience through observability, runbooks and automated recovery.

  • Practical experience designing event-driven, distributed systems and navigating the trade-offs that come with eventual consistency at scale.

  • Background in a fast-moving, product-led environment where commercial impact drives decisions and adapting quickly is part of the job.

  • A track record of creating the conditions for engineers to step up, not just mentoring but actively giving ownership and space to grow.

WHAT WE OFFER (in addition to a competitive salary)

  • 25 days of holiday (+ Bank Holidays) 🏖

  • Share Incentive Plan 📈

  • Workplace Pension 💰

  • Private Medical Insurance 🏥 (including Dental 🦷 Optical 👓 & Mental Health 💆‍♀️ support options)

  • Various Salary Sacrifice Schemes - Holiday Purchase, Tech, Gym, Cycle to Work, Electric Vehicle, Private Medical Insurance for families 💵

  • Enhanced Parental Leave and Pay 🐣

  • £1000 toward relevant professional qualifications 🎓

  • £500 per annum towards learning and development 🌱

  • 3 days paid leave for L&D purposes 🌻

We work hybrid, typically three days a week in our Central London office (fewer office days can be accommodated for longer commute times), a few minutes from Moorgate and Liverpool Street. Visits to client sites, conferences and broker offices count towards office days.

ONE LAST THING..

Authenticity is important to us. We value the unique qualities and experiences you bring. So if you apply, just be your genuine self. It’s who we want!

What you’ll be doing

  • Help unlock growth in new market segments, including emerging mobility.

  • Collate and analyse portfolio data so our Head of Motor Underwriting can track performance.

data.title: Senior Product Manager
data.description:
Our mission is to enable everyone to build wealth

We reinvent how trading and investing work by creating exceptional products people love. Fostering a culture of excellence and high velocity is the key to our success. Тoday, we serve over 6 million clients, with more than €38 billion in assets under management — a testament to the scale and trust we’ve built in just a few years.

The role

You'll own a product area end to end, including its legal and regulatory position. We're hiring across trading and execution (order routing, settlement, corporate actions), tax-efficient investing and pensions (ISAs, SIPPs and German pension accounts), crypto, and client accounts and payments (onboarding, client money, cards and FX). You work directly with your engineers, designers, Legal, Compliance, and Operations, and answer for both the client experience and the commercial result.

What you'll do

  • Decide what your area builds next, from client needs, product data and commercial goals, and defend the choice

  • Read the regulation, the API documentation and the operational process yourself, and form the position before Legal and Compliance review it

  • Write the spec: client journey, business rules, data, integrations and acceptance criteria, detailed enough to build and test from

  • Carry your decisions through delivery with Engineering, Design, Legal, Compliance and Operations

  • Take the product through testing and launch, then run it: monitoring, client feedback, the numbers, the next improvement

What you need to have

  • A complex product you shipped yourself and can walk through in detail, including where it broke: a rounding rule, a time zone, a position you argued, an API that changed under you

  • Enough technical understanding to read documentation, follow a data flow and reason about system behaviour with engineers

  • Your own numbers: you query the data yourself and can explain every figure you quote

  • Regular use of AI in product work, checked against documentation, data and other primary sources

What we offer:

  • An area that is yours, including its legal position, with more engineering capacity than most product teams get

  • A co-founder in your interview loop and in your work

  • Challenges that will help you grow and realize your potential fast

  • Opportunity to make a significant impact —you will build innovative services used by millions of investors to build wealth

  • Work with smart, spirited, helpful, high-performing colleagues with a common goal

  • An environment where nothing is set in stone

  • Appreciation for your talent and ideas

  • Generous remuneration package

Bring your ambition to Europe’s fastest-growing mobile broker!

We thank all applicants, but only candidates selected for interview will be contacted. All personal data of applicants is protected by law and treated with strict confidentiality.

data.title: Chief of Staff
data.description:
Powering Great Work

We started as the place to find a trusted trade. Now, as we shape the future of home improvement, we're building the tech to transform that landscape for everyone - better products, smarter data, AI where it actually helps - so trades can spend less time on admin and consumers can find someone they trust, first time. That's Powering Great Work, and it's why every team here exists:

🔧 Trades spend less time on admin and more on winning work and growing their business

🏠 Homeowners get a trusted trade, first time, every time

🚀 We get to build products that change homes and lives across the country

As our next Chief of Staff, you'll be right at the heart of how our leadership team runs. Working side by side with our Director of Strategy & Corporate Development, CEO and the wider exec team, you'll make sure the right things get in front of the right people at the right time, from briefings and meeting prep across the business and with our external partners, to the rhythm of Board and leadership meetings. You'll also use AI to change how that team works. If you can take a messy situation, bring order to it and come back with a clear view, you'll be trusted from day one.

The job, unfiltered

  • Run the leadership operating rhythm: own the reporting agenda, leadership meeting and Board packs, KPI tracking and action follow-up, so it all runs without anyone needing to chase.

  • Join the CEO's briefings and prepare meetings across the business and with external partners, bringing the analysis and a clear point of view so he and the exec team can spend their time where it counts.

  • Step in on the tough cross-functional questions no one else has time for, and take them all the way to a clear recommendation, working with our Director of Strategy & Corporate Development.

  • Help shape the story we tell investors and the quarterly Board agenda, alongside the CEO, Director of Strategy & Corporate Development and CFO.

  • Support our strategic growth agenda, from market mapping to planning how we bring new businesses into the fold with our operating teams.

  • Put AI to work: build agents for the CEO's and leadership team's day-to-day workflows (think meeting prep, action tracking and KPI monitoring) and help us work out how agents change our market.

The fit

  • Sound judgement and real discretion: you'll be trusted with confidential and sensitive information, and you form a view, say it plainly and change it when the evidence does.

  • Brilliant at bringing order: you juggle competing priorities, keep many things moving at once and keep senior people one step ahead, without needing to be chased.

  • Thrives with ownership: you can pick up an unclear brief, move at pace in ambiguous situations, own it end to end and bring peers and senior stakeholders with you without formal authority.

  • Clear writing and structured, numerate thinking: you can turn a messy question into a one-page recommendation. (This isn't a finance role.)

  • AI-native: you use AI tools daily, have built something with them and want to change how a team works. A background in consulting or an operating role (strategy and operations, growth, product or commercial at a tech company) is a great start.

(Don't self-select out because you don't tick every box. We'd rather meet you.)

What You Get

💰 Competitive salary, annual bonus & equity scheme

🩺 Health, wellbeing and learning support

🚲 Wellhub, Smart Tech Scheme, Cycle Scheme, Season ticket loan

🎂 Birthday/special day leave, buy & sell holiday scheme

❤️ 1 week's paid charity leave, and more

How This Goes

  • Screening call with one of our Talent Acquisition Partners

  • 1st stage: interview with Rich Bolton, Director, Strategy & Corporate Development

  • Final stage: interview with Jambu Palaniappan, our CEO

We’re growing fast, with big plans to become the go-to brand for home improvements. If you care about great work, take pride in the details, and want to make an impact, you’ll fit right in.

The Role

We're looking for a Senior Revenue Operations Manager to join our Revenue Operations team and act as a broad, senior partner to our revenue organisation. You'll run the complex analysis and modelling behind target setting and annual planning for the entire commercial organisation. You will also help the Director set and execute the revenue analytics strategy, and run the insights that shape how revenue leadership sees the business. As you ramp up, you will take on growing ownership of the forecasting cadence alongside the Director of Revenue Operations.

We are looking for someone with very strong analytical and modelling skills, which are the foundation of the role, especially in your first two quarters. Just as important, we want someone who is commercially minded and keen to grow into a generalist role, broadening from there into revenue insights and forecasting.


What You’ll Do

  • First 90 days: Scope the revenue analytics strategy and build the core dashboards.

  • First 180 days: Lead the analysis for the annual planning and target-setting cycle, and automate the core of revenue reporting and insights with AI tooling.

  • First 12 months: Take on co-ownership of the forecasting cadence with the Director of Revenue Operations.

 

What Will You Be Doing?

Run Complex Modelling & Analysis

  • Run complex analysis and modelling to support target setting and the annual planning process for the entire commercial organisation, made up of around 600 commercial roles across SDRs, AEs and Account Managers.

  • Build and maintain the models behind target setting: capacity, quota and productivity assumptions, and territory and segment allocation.

  • Frame the key planning questions, choose the method, pressure-test scenarios and sensitivities, and deliver clear recommendations to revenue leadership, explaining the trade-offs in plain language.

  • Work as the senior analytical partner to the other analyst on the team: stay hands-on in the models while setting the quality bar and documentation standards, so each planning cycle is repeatable and auditable.

Build the Revenue Analytics Strategy

  • Partner with the Director of Revenue Operations to define the revenue analytics strategy: what we need to build across Salesforce and Looker, and in what order.

  • Map the current reporting landscape — what exists, what's trusted, what's duplicated or out of date — and use that map to shape the build plan.

  • Own execution of that plan: build and maintain the core dashboards and reports that revenue leadership and the wider commercial organisation rely on.

  • Launch and run a recurring insights digest for revenue leaders, turning dashboards and data into a clear narrative — what changed, why it matters, what to do about it.

  • Bring a point of view on what's worth building versus what's noise, and be willing to push back on requests that don't earn their keep.

AI at Perk
AI is embedded in how we work across every function. The tools you'll use day-to-day are AI-enabled so you can move faster and spend more time on the work that matters. In practice, that means using AI to research and prioritise accounts, draft and refine outreach, handle customer interactions more effectively, synthesise information, and cut through shadow work - the invisible tasks that pull people away from the work only they can do - so you can focus on relationships and outcomes.

At Perk, we take an IRL-first approach to work, where our team works together in-person 3 days a week. As such, this role requires you to be based within commuting distance of our hubs. We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work.

For certain roles, we can help with relocation from anywhere in the world, English is the official language at the office. Please submit your resume in English if you choose to apply. Do not forget to submit an updated portfolio and/or resume.

Protect Yourself from Recruitment Scams

All official communication from Perk will always come from email addresses ending in @perk.com or @externalperk.com, our verified social media channels, or recruiters listed on our official LinkedIn page. data.title: AI software Engineer - Project Tricorder
data.description:
Project Tricorder — Clinical Infrastructure for Field Operations

We're looking for a hands-on engineer to build two foundations of the Tricorder product: the evaluation harness and training data pipeline behind our AI models, and a clinical knowledge base grounded in tactical combat care, SNOMED CT and ICD-10.

About Project Tricorder - https://www.tricorder-systems.com/

Most healthcare technology assumes a hospital: reliable power, connectivity and a clinician at a desk. Care increasingly happens somewhere else - in the field, in transit, in remote and contested environments, and in the critical minutes before a patient reaches a ward.

Tricorder builds the deployable clinical infrastructure for that world: a rugged, self-contained hardware and software platform that lets clinical teams capture, monitor and act on patient data anywhere, even when the network or the grid can't be relied on. It is a dual-use venture serving defence medical and civilian pre-hospital care.

Our prototype product is already in user testing. Edge AI sits at the core: multimodal language models that turn video, sensor data and clinical notes into patient records, drive predictions and inform data-driven learnings across deployments. To trust those models in the field, we need rigorous data and evaluation - that's where you come in.

What you'll do

You'll own two workstreams, working day to day with the founder and the FF build team.

1. Data pipeline and evaluation harness

Build the data foundations that tell us whether our models are good enough for clinical use.

  • Data labelling: design labelling schemas and guidelines, set up tooling, and run labelling with clinical input, including quality checks and inter-annotator agreement.

  • Data processing: build reproducible pipelines to ingest, clean, de-identify and transform multimodal data (video, sensor streams, text).

  • Video data organisation: structure, version and catalogue video datasets so clips, annotations and metadata stay searchable and traceable.

  • Training dataset preparation: assemble balanced, well-documented train, validation and test splits, with clear lineage from raw data to model input.

  • Eval harness: build an automated harness that benchmarks vision-language and NLP models against clinically meaningful metrics, tracks regressions and supports build-vs-buy model decisions.

2. Clinical knowledge base

Build the structured clinical knowledge base that turns unstructured input into coded, interoperable records.

  • Database design: design the schema and stand up the data store for clinical concepts and their relationships.

  • Clinical terminologies: ingest and map TC3, SNOMED CT, ICD-10 and related NHS standards, including cross-mappings between them.

  • Natural language processing: extract entities and relationships from clinical text and link them to coded concepts.

  • Document handling: parse and structure clinical documents (PDFs, notes, forms) into the database.

  • Clinical knowledge: work with clinicians to make sure the database reflects real-world clinical reasoning and pre-hospital workflows.

By the end of the first 3 months, we'd expect a working eval harness in use for model decisions, a labelled and versioned core dataset, and a first version of the knowledge base linked to the product.

What we're looking for

We don't expect one person to be expert in everything below. Strong candidates will be deep in one workstream and credible in the other.

Must-haves

  • Strong Python and data engineering skills, with a track record of shipping production data or ML pipelines, not just research notebooks.

  • Hands-on experience building ML evaluation frameworks, benchmarks or test harnesses, ideally for vision, video or language models.

  • Experience running data labelling and training-data preparation, including annotation tooling and quality control.

  • Working knowledge of databases and data modelling.

  • Practical NLP experience: entity extraction, entity linking or document parsing.

  • Comfort handling sensitive data under data protection and clinical safety constraints.

  • Pragmatism and speed: you can work with ambiguity, make good build-vs-buy calls and ship in weeks, not quarters.

Nice to have

  • Experience with SNOMED CT, ICD-10, dm+d or other NHS clinical terminologies and coding.

  • A background in health-tech, clinical informatics or another regulated domain such as defence.

  • Experience with video data at scale (frame sampling, temporal annotation, multimodal datasets).

  • Familiarity with FHIR or HL7 interoperability standards.

  • Experience working with LLMs and VLMs, including edge or on-device deployment.

  • Early-stage startup experience, especially as a founding or early engineer.

Probably not the right fit if

  • You need detailed specs and a large team around you to be effective.

  • You prefer pure research over building tools people use every day.

This is a high urgency opening, and we are flexible to consider applicants either on a more flexible consultancy agreement (rolling by mutual agreement, with a competitive day rate); or a long term permanent employment contract with shares as part of the package and scope to grow into a longer-term role as Tricorder builds its engineering team.

data.title: Fractional Chief Medical Officer  - Tricorder Systems
data.description:
Fractional Chief Medical Officer — Project Tricorder

We're looking for a clinician who has served as a military medic to be Tricorder's clinical lead and the medical name behind the product. You'll shape clinical workflows, protect patient safety, help to roadmap clinical device regulation, giving the product credibility with clinicians, defence customers and investors.

About Project Tricorder - https://www.tricorder-systems.com/

Most healthcare technology assumes a hospital: reliable power, connectivity and a clinician at a desk. But the moments that decide outcomes often happen elsewhere: at the point of injury, in transit, in remote and contested environments, and in the critical minutes before a patient reaches a ward.

Tricorder is building deployable clinical infrastructure for that world. It's a rugged, self-contained hardware and software platform that lets clinical teams capture, monitor and act on patient data anywhere, even when the network or the grid can't be relied on. It's a dual-use venture serving defence medical first and civilian pre-hospital and humanitarian care next.

Tricorder is being built inside Founders Factory's venture studio, with dedicated pre-seed investment and a six-month build programme. The founder, a former British Army officer, is in place, the founding engineer is incoming, and a few more team hires are underway.

What you'll do

You'll be Tricorder's senior clinical voice: the person who makes sure what we build works for a medic at the point of injury and keeps patients safe.

  • Shape clinical workflows: map how casualties are assessed, treated, handed over and evacuated, from the point of injury through to definitive care. Turn that into product requirements, and test prototypes against real resuscitation and trauma scenarios.

  • Protect patient safety: lead clinical risk management and act as (or help appoint) the Clinical Safety Officer under the NHS DCB0129 standard. Advise on the evidence needed for the medical device and regulatory pathway.

  • Be the medical face of the product: put your clinical name to Tricorder. Represent it to defence medical services, NHS and ambulance trusts, humanitarian organisations and investors, and help the founder carry the clinical story in pitches and pilots.

  • Open doors: use your network across defence medicine, the NHS and humanitarian response to secure clinical pilots, user testing and early design partners.

  • Guide clinical evidence: help design pilots and early studies, and review clinical claims, protocols and terminology across the product and its AI features.

  • Advise the team: be a sounding board for the founder and build team on clinical priorities. Help with clinical hiring as the company grows.

Who you are

Must-haves

  • You've served as a military medic or doctor. This is non-negotiable. You know operational medicine first-hand, from point-of-injury care to the field hospital.

  • A GMC-registered doctor with deep experience in resuscitation, trauma or emergency surgery, emergency medicine, or pre-hospital care.

  • Still active clinically, whether as a reservist, in the NHS, or in humanitarian or disaster response.

  • You're credible with senior defence medical leaders, NHS clinicians and investors, and comfortable being the named clinical lead for a product.

  • You can turn clinical reality into clear, practical product decisions, and you're happy working with engineers and designers at startup pace.

Nice to have

  • Experience advising or working with medtech or health-tech startups, ideally as a CMO, clinical lead or advisor.

  • Clinical Safety Officer training (DCB0129/DCB0160), or experience with medical device regulation (UKCA/CE, ISO 14971).

  • Leadership roles in defence medical services, such as a clinical lead, medical director or command role.

  • Experience with mass-casualty planning, deployed hospital care, or global health systems.

  • Familiarity with clinical AI, data standards or digital health interoperability.

Probably not the right fit if

  • You haven't served in a military medical role.

  • You're looking for a passive advisory title without hands-on involvement in the product.

Fire, Health & Safety Consultant - Contractor/Associate

Ark Workplace Risk | Competitive Day Rate 

 

At Ark Workplace Risk, we empower our clients to confidently manage risk, compliance, and safety through a trusted partnership built on expert knowledge, innovative solutions, and proactive guidance and insight.

 

About Ark Workplace Risk: 

Proven Expert Knowledge: With over 30 years of experience and a trusted reputation among 200+ UK organisations, we provide workable solutions that align with our clients' organisational and business goals, as well as regulatory requirements.

Industry-Leading Software: Our innovative tools streamline risk and compliance management, putting clients in control and enabling them to demonstrate accountability to stakeholders.

Insight-Driven Solutions: As industry thought leaders, we provide actionable insights into emerging legislation, guidance, and industry trends, ensuring court-readiness for their business.

Responsive Partnership: From every day, business-as-usual guidance to urgent, critical, complex, and contentious scenarios, we work in partnership with clients, becoming their trusted advisor and solution provider, whenever and wherever they need us most.

 

Responsibilities: 

 

  • Undertake risk assessments including fire and health and safety, ensuring the fee earning target is met. 
  • Undertake various fire, health and safety assignments within your competency.
  • Deliver client reports within the agreed SLA, in accordance with a forensic and pragmatic approach to ensure the Ark 'Gold Standard' is achieved. 
  • Design health and safety site management systems where required, specific to client requirements.
  • Undertake onsite briefings and advise on risk management improvements.
  • Work collaboratively with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders.
  • Work with other consultants to ensure we are constantly sharing knowledge across the team.
  • Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of controlling risks, compliances etc. in relation to our online management system QUOODA®

 

The ideal candidate will have:

  • At least 2+ years' fire, health & safety risk assessment experience within the built environment in residential and/or commercial buildings
  • Good working knowledge of Approved Document B
  • Good working knowledge of BS 9999 / 9997
  • Education suitable to be competent to carry out Fire and Health & Safety risk assessments on seven or more floors
  • The ability to undertake Fire Risk Assessments and General Risk Assessments at the same time
  • Articulate and clear communicators and report writing abilities as well as a comprehensive understanding of current UK regulations

 

Qualifications

  • Must have NEBOSH General Certificate in Health & Safety or equivalent as minimum.
  • Must have a minimum of a level 3 in fire safety/fire risk
  • Recognised fire safety memberships e.g. AIFireE, MIFireE, GIFireE, MIFSM etc.
  • Willing to apply for or have registered on any of the following fire risk assessors registers IFSM, FRACS, IFPO or IFE

 

Practical Requirements: 

Ability to facilitate hybrid working with home office that is suitable for connectivity to the office and clients, a safe and productive place to work conducive for delivering daily duties.

data.title: Full Stack Engineer
data.description:
Getting homes off fossil fuels means fitting millions of heat pumps, solar panels and batteries, and every one has to be designed, sold and fitted by an installer. The assets themselves already work brilliantly, but getting them into homes is still slow, complex and painful. Our mission is to change that: to make it wildly easier and more profitable to run a renewables installation business, and get homes off fossil fuels way faster.

In just a few years we've become the leading platform for heat pump installers in the UK and Ireland, with around half of all heat pump installations now being managed on Spruce. We've just launched our solar and battery product, and we're building on that to go after even bigger opportunities: every other type of job these installers do, the rest of how they run their business, and a bunch of new countries.

We're now on the hunt for truly brilliant engineers to help us move faster and go further.

 

🌲 About Spruce

  • Almost 20% of the UK's carbon emissions comes from heating homes – there's simply no way to reach net zero without phasing out gas and oil boilers. Right now the only serious alternative is heat pumps, with their almost-magical ability to turn 1 kW of electricity into 3-5 kW of heat (🤯). But the heat pump installation journey is slow, inefficient, and just so painful. This makes it hard for existing installers to grow their businesses and puts off gas engineers from starting to do heat pumps. Perhaps most critically, it means you can't currently offer a heat pump when someone's boiler breaks and they urgently need heating.

  • We're fixing this. We've built a platform for heat pump installers to manage the whole installation journey from initial enquiry through to final compliance paperwork, freeing up their time to focus on what really matters: doing high-quality installations, providing great customer service, and scaling their business. Despite only getting started at the beginning of 2024, we're having a massive impact on installation businesses, suppliers, and manufacturers across the UK: halving the time they spend on each job and doubling their sales conversion rates.

  • We raised a chunky Seed round last year from top-tier investors and this year have doubled the team and grown revenue 4x. We've expanded into Ireland, have just launched an end-to-end solar and battery product, and are increasingly becoming the operating system for the whole home renewables supply chain. If you can picture a combination of ServiceTitan, Procore, and AutoCAD, you might get a sense of where we're headed…

 

🥖 The Role

You'll work closely with a small, high-calibre team of engineers, designers and domain experts to build and scale the tools that power our installer software, owning and delivering complex features end-to-end from day one.

The problem space is deep and varied, including:

  • Heat loss modelling and hydronic system design

  • 2D and 3D floor-plan tooling using LiDAR and computer vision

  • Large-scale data ingestion and geospatial analysis

  • Offline-first, collaborative PWAs

  • Hardware integrations (Bluetooth measurement tools, sensors, monitoring systems)

This is not CRUD-only work. You'll be working on meaningful production problems from day one that blend physical reality, real-world constraints, and serious impact.

 

🥞 Tech Stack

Our tech stack strives for simplicity, symmetry and efficiency. Our hard problems come from the real world instead of self-made architectural problems.

You don't need to know all of the below, but you do need an appetite for full stack mastery and owning the problem end to end:

  • Docker, Docker Compose

  • PostgreSQL, PostGIS, Atlas migrations

  • Node, Prisma

  • React, TypeScript, Konva, Tailwind

 

🫵 About You

We look for the same five things in everyone at Spruce: curiosity; intense drive, ambition and work ethic; a high degree of personal agency and ownership; deep humility and a growth mindset; and excellent craft.

We're hiring at mid-level: you've probably been shipping production code for a few years. We care less about titles and more about impact, judgment, and intent. You'll likely have experience with:

  • Modern JavaScript / TypeScript and frontend frameworks

  • Backend development and API design

  • Relational databases and data modelling

But more importantly, you are:

  • Product-minded – you want to understand real users and real problems, not just tickets;

  • Impact-driven – you balance technical quality with momentum and know when "good enough" is exactly right;

  • Comfortable with ownership – you take responsibility for outcomes, not just code;

  • Candid and collaborative – you challenge ideas openly, receive feedback well, and optimise for the team over ego;

  • Already using AI intensively – you use it every day to make yourself disproportionately more effective, and you can show us how.

… and you'll hopefully also love heat pumps! 🤓

 

🌟 Our offer

  • 💰 £50–100k salary, depending on experience

  • 🍰 Equity (options) in the company

  • 🏡 Hybrid working: 2 days in-person a week (London or Bristol), with full-team meetups every fortnight

  • 🏖️ 33 days holiday (25 plus bank holidays) and opportunity to work from abroad for another 30 days each year

  • 🏥 Private Medical Cover (Vitality)

  • 👧 Workplace Nursery Benefit scheme (YellowNest)

  • 🧑‍🍼 Enhanced Parental Leave

  • 🚲 Cycle to Work scheme

  • 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Brilliant team to learn from and massive opportunity to grow

 

🧑‍💻 Working at Spruce

  • We're currently a close-knit team of 35, split between London and Bristol. We spend 2–3 days each week working together in-person in both locations, and get everyone together every fortnight.

  • You'll have genuine influence from day one. The best idea wins regardless of seniority. We expect you to challenge everything, ask "why?" multiple levels deep, and push back when something doesn't make sense.

  • We want everyone to spend time with installers on-site, feel their pain points, then rapidly suggest and implement solutions based on real feedback rather than assumptions.

  • We move fast and ship imperfect things, learning from users rather than trying to perfect in isolation. When things break, we focus on how we fix it and what we can learn – and never blame. You'll own your outcomes whilst knowing the team has your back.

  • Feedback is constant, direct, and kind – we'll tell you when something isn't working and expect the same honesty (and empathy) back.

About Kaluza

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.


What you’ll do

You’ll protect service quality and client trust at Kaluza by making sure Major Incidents are handled well, root causes are properly investigated, and lasting fixes happen across the platform.

  • Step in as Deputy during Major Incidents, helping to start up the response team and keep it running

  • Attend Major Incident post-mortems, making sure improvement actions are captured and owned

  • Write clear, client-facing Post Incident Reports that set out post-mortem findings and agreed improvements

  • Monitor the health of the Incident Management process across so we consistently meet our contractual SLAs

  • Lead Kaluza’s Problem Management practice: uncover the underlying causes of incidents, get them into Product Team backlogs, and track workarounds

  • Prepare and deliver regular Problem Management reviews, and support incident reviews, with clients and internal teams

  • Keep improving how we run Incident and Problem Management


What you’ll bring

Essential criteria:

  • Experience leading or working within Major Incident response teams

  • Experience using Incident and Problem Management processes in a Service Operations environment

  • Experience using Jira


Ideally, you’ll have:

  • Experience working in an ITIL-aligned service management environment

  • Experience using Jira beyond ticket management, e.g. building dashboards and creating or managing workflows and automations

  • Experience turning technical findings into clear, professional client-facing updates and reports

  • Experience using data and metrics to influence teams

  • Experience in a utilities, energy or SaaS platform environment

Tech stack: Jira

 

Our Values

Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:

  • Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.

  • Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.

  • Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.

  • Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.

  • Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.

 

Our Perks

  • Time off and family: 26 days’ holiday, plus 26 weeks’ full pay for new parents with no qualifying service period

  • Health and security: Private medical insurance with virtual GP, life assurance, pension scheme, free mortgage advice and eye tests

  • Pay and flexibility: Discretionary bonus, a Flex Fund of 5% [of salary] to spend on the benefits you want most, retail discounts through Perks at Work

  • Growth and setup: Personal learning budget, home office budget

  • Climate: Furthr, our climate action app

Come as you are

We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.

data.title: Agency Lead - Middle Mile
data.description:
Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~160 people, around half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

The Opportunity

Every morning before most of the country is awake, Relay's middle mile moves parcels in vans from our sort centres to thousands of local shops we call pitstops. A big share of those vans and drivers come from partner agencies, which makes them one of the most important partnerships in the business. When an agency doesn't show up, or we simply don't have enough, parcels don't move, couriers wait and customers feel it that same day. When a contract is wrong, it hits our P&L directly.

Right now our agency relationships run on ad hoc calls handled by our live support team. You'll be the person who changes that. You'll build proper account management from scratch, with clear standards, regular reviews and real consequences when standards slip. You'll make sure we always have enough reliable, compliant capacity at a price that works, and a bench of agencies ready to step in when one doesn't deliver. As we open new sort centres across the UK and expand internationally, you'll be the one finding and launching the agency partners that get each new region moving from day one. You won't just manage the process, you'll help rebuild it. You'll work side by side with our engineers to design a better experience for agencies and automate the manual work out of it.

As engineering automations go live and more of the middle mile runs itself, the role grows with it. The playbook you build here becomes the blueprint for every new market we enter. It can widen into a Marketplace Partnerships Lead across all our supply: van and moped rental deals, background check and onboarding suppliers, local partnerships in areas where we need more couriers, and courier benefits programmes.

Outcomes you own

  • Agency shift fill. Agencies reliably fill the shifts gave to them, including at short notice and through peak.

  • Agency driver attendance and quality. Agency drivers turn up for the shifts they accept, on time, trained and ready at the sort centre.

  • Agency cost per shift. Rates and bonuses stay within budget, and every pound of premium we pay an agency earns its place.

  • Agency supply pool. Each agency keeps enough onboarded drivers to ramp with us. An agency running the same four drivers every day has no flex.

  • A healthy agency bench. Every agency knows how it ranks against our standards and its peers, and we always have a replacement ready for one that persistently underperforms.

What you’ll do

  1. Own every agency relationship. Be the single point of contact for all our middle mile driver agencies. Run weekly account calls, step in fast when performance dips, and build relationships that hold up on the hardest peak mornings.

  2. Hold agencies to account. Track fill, attendance and driver quality for every agency and share it with them. When one falls short, find out why: separate what’s on us (route length, late shift release) from what’s on them (no-shows, hand-backs), and agree a fix with a target, a date and an owner. Fix the cause rather than paying more to cover it.

  3. Own contracts, rates and terms. Negotiate rates, bonuses and contract terms. Use data to compare agencies before every rate conversation, and know when to walk away from a deal that doesn’t work for us.

  4. Build the bench. Source, vet and contract new agencies in each region. Start them small, scale the ones that deliver and replace the ones that don’t, so we’re never dependent on one low performer.

  5. Be the escalation point. Live Ops handles day-to-day shift fill. When an agency misses its agreement, is unhappy with how we’re working with them, or sort centre teams see a pattern of problems with its drivers, you resolve it.

  6. Shape new ways of working. We’re automating how agencies receive and book shifts. Be the expert on what works for agencies, advise Product and Engineering on the designs, and move every agency onto the new process.

What you’ll need

  • Ownership. You run outcomes, not tasks. A good week is one where agency fill, attendance and cost move the right way.

  • Hands-on ops experience. You’ve worked in logistics, delivery, transport or a similar fast-moving operation, and can run the operational work yourself rather than hand it off.

  • Supplier or account management. You’ve managed agencies, subcontractors or a third-party workforce, ideally with commercial targets attached.

  • Comfort with hard conversations. You hold partners to what they agreed, challenge excuses and keep the relationship intact.

  • Ops judgement under pressure. At 05:30 with a van broken down, you work out what’s most at risk, make the call and tell the right people what happens next.

  • Comfort with data. You can turn a volume plan into shifts per day by site, read a dashboard and question a number. Spreadsheets are a must; SQL is a plus.

  • Comfort with ambiguity. This is a new role in a fast-growing network. You’ll shape how it works rather than inherit a playbook.

Fast and focused hiring process

  1. Talent Acquisition interview – 30 mins

  2. Hiring Manager interview – 45 mins

  3. Case interview: live role plays of real agency situations – 1 hour

Decision and offer within 48 hours. Our process mirrors our pace of work.

Who Thrives at Relay?

  • Aim with Precision: You define problems clearly and measure your impact meticulously.

  • Play to Win: You chase bold bets, tackle the hard stuff, and view constraints as fuel, not friction.

  • 1% Better Every Day: You believe that small, consistent improvements lead to exponential growth. You move quickly, deliver results, and learn from every experience.

  • All In, All the Time: You show up and step up. You take ownership from start to finish and do what it takes to deliver when it counts.

  • People-Powered Greatness: You invest in your teammates. You give and receive feedback with care and candour. You build trust through high standards and shared success.

  • Grow the Whole Pie: You seek out win-win solutions for merchants, couriers, and our customers, because when they thrive, so do we.

    If these resonate, and you combine strong technical fundamentals with entrepreneurial drive, let’s connect.

Relay is an equal-opportunity employer committed to diversity, inclusion, and fostering a workplace where everyone thrives.

data.description:
About Zable

Zable (formerly Lendable) is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money.

  • Founded in 2014, profitable since 2017, unicorn since 2021

  • The number one issuer of new credit cards and loans in the UK

  • Backed by Balderton Capital and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan

  • Loved by customers & our team with top reviews on Glassdoor and Trustpilot

Zable was founded on the belief that smarter technology is the solution to lower cost, more transparent consumer finance. Our proprietary foundation models analyse thousands of data points in seconds, drawing a more complete picture of individual financial behaviour. This means we can make better risk decisions, widening access and lowering prices.

The Zable credit card harnesses this technology to deliver better borrowing for three million people. Through our superapp, Zable connects this card to a single platform which makes it effortless to manage credit, get a loan, refinance existing borrowing, switch utilities, get a mobile plan and save more.

Zable is now the number one issuer of new credit cards and personal loans in the UK, but we’ve barely got started. Next, we’re taking our approach to some of the biggest markets in the world - the US and Mexico - where hundreds of millions of people are underserved by outdated bank processes.

Join us if you want to

  • Take ownership across a broad remit - you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Zable from day one

  • Work in small teams of exceptional people - who are relentlessly resourceful to solve problems and find smarter solutions than the status quo

  • Build the best technology in-house - using new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

 

What you'll do

Strategic Financial Planning: Collaborating with senior management to develop and execute treasury strategies aligned with our business objectives. You will provide expert guidance on liquidity management, capital allocation, and risk mitigation to optimize our financial performance.

Treasury Operations: Overseeing the operational aspects of treasury, including cash management, foreign exchange, and hedging activities. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to streamline processes, enhance efficiency, and leverage technology to automate treasury operations.

Cash Flow Management: Overseeing the day-to-day cash flow operations, including forecasting, monitoring, and reporting. You will ensure that our liquidity needs are met efficiently, minimizing idle cash and maximizing investment opportunities.

Treasury Portfolio Management: Work with Capital Markets to establish optimum investment strategy for Treasury assets. Source, evaluate and manage portfolio investments.

Risk Management: Implementing robust risk management practices to safeguard our financial position. You will assess and mitigate financial risks, such as interest rate, liquidity, and credit risks, while ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements in both the UK and US markets.

Stakeholder Management: Building and maintaining strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including regulators, auditors, and investors. You will effectively communicate our treasury strategies, financial performance, and risk management practices to ensure transparency and trust.

Team Leadership: Leading and developing a lean high-performing treasury team, fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement. You will provide guidance, mentorship, and support to empower your team members to excel in their roles.

What we’re looking for

  • Extensive experience in treasury management, preferably within the consumer lending, asset management or banking sectors.

  • Strong knowledge of UK and US financial markets, regulations, and best practices.

  • Proven track record in strategic financial planning, cash flow management, and risk mitigation.

  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to make data-driven decisions.

  • Expertise in treasury operations and systems implementation and management.

  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence and build relationships at all levels.

  • Strong leadership capabilities, with a passion for developing and motivating teams.

  • Excited about the opportunity to work in an entrepreneurial environment and have a real impact on the business

Life at Zable
